title: Typed XRECORD DXF coordinate-base preflight with extension compatibility
mode: local fast implementation slice with generated ASCII/Binary controls
scope: Keep typed XRECORD point tuples anchored at an X-coordinate group
Preserve existing local extended XRECORD handle-value behavior
Preserve raw-object replay as a distinct provenance-gated contract

sources.title: Autodesk XRECORD (DXF)
sources.supports: The documented XRECORD standard profile uses normal object group codes in the 1-369 range, excluding identity codes 5 and 105; this is not used as a blanket filter for existing local extension routes.

sources.title: Autodesk DXF Group Codes for Xrecords
sources.supports: The XRECORD point/vector payload is assigned to group codes 10-17.

sources.title: Autodesk DXF Group Codes in Numerical Order
sources.supports: Groups 20-27 and 30-37 carry Y/Z components for the documented point families; they are not independent X bases.

sources.title: Local XRECORD reader and Wave 1 writer contract
sources.supports: The local parser has extended point/handle code families, and the existing typed XRECORD writer control requires 480/481 values to survive.

implementation.summary: Typed XRECORD COORD variants are checked before handle reservation or record emission: their code must be an X component with valid Y/Z followers in the same point family used by DRW_XRecord::parseCode. Existing extended scalar/string/handle group routes remain unchanged; raw-captured object replay remains separate.
implementation.wireBehaviorDetail: A COORD variant supplied at a Y/Z component or incomplete point family now fails before output instead of being expanded as a shifted or unparseable point. No overall 1-369 code cap is imposed, preserving the existing 480/481 handle route.

generatedControls.asciiAndBinaryNegative: Typed coordinate bases 18, 20, 30, and 38 are refused while preserving an existing destination sentinel.
generatedControls.asciiAndBinaryPositive: Point base 17 writes and reads back the expected XYZ values; the paired Wave 1 suite retains the 480/481 handle extension control.

results.owningCtests: passed (2/2): Wave 1 and DXF fixtures; Wave 1 retained the code 480/481 XRECORD control

assessment.localMismatchFound: The typed XRECORD DXF writer expanded a COORD variant at any supplied group code, including Y/Z component codes that the local parser interprets as components rather than a point base.
assessment.claim: Typed COORD values must start at a complete X component within the existing parser's point-family map. Extended group-code behavior remains as before; no support claim is promoted.
assessment.limitations: The Autodesk XRECORD reference describes a narrower standard group-code profile than some existing local typed reader/writer routes, including the tested 480/481 handle values. An initial blanket cap was reverted after the Wave 1 owner test exposed that compatibility contract. This slice deliberately preserves those routes; it does not resolve their independent interoperability status, validate every XRECORD schema, cover DWG XRECORD encoding, qualify raw replay, native CAD acceptance, or establish cross-version behavior.
